_note: Character creation background questions (GDD 4.1.1, 'Built (points pool)'). effects are added to the starting attributes (1-20 scale); every answer's visible effects are a profile (strengths paid by weaknesses), not free strength. experience = years of organised training behind the answer: the points pool is pool.base + the sum of experience (6-16), and each experience point above pool.neutral_experience lowers trainability by pool.trainability_per_experience (below it raises it): a trained body starts stronger but has fewer easy gains left.

pool._note: base + experience = points to spend in the Attributes step; max_per_attribute = cap per attribute. Trainability shift = (neutral_experience - experience) * trainability_per_experience; every physical attribute also moves by (experience - neutral_experience) * physical_per_experience (years of training show in the body).

estimate._note: The coach's guess on the Attributes step and the summary: the 800 m time from the athlete's ability now, and where that sits among the rivals of the same age and gender (percentile of Data.races.rivals at the start). Bands are upper limits of the percentile.
estimate.line: Coach's guess: about %s for 800 m right now.
bands: That's near the back of most fields for now. Plenty of room to grow.
That would put you in the slower half of a local meet.
That's around the middle of the %s who race the 800 m.
That would put you in the faster half of a local meet.
That's near the front of local meets already.
estimate.pool_text: Your points come from your story: every bit of organised training behind you adds some. More training means a stronger start but fewer easy gains left; beginners improve faster.
estimate.weight_legend: Dots show how much an attribute counts for your 800 m time.
weight_tiers: Counts a lot for your 800 m time.
Counts quite a bit for your 800 m time.
Counts a little for your 800 m time.
estimate.weight_none: Doesn't go straight into your 800 m time: it works through training, recovery or your race decisions.

questions.question: What did you do before athletics?

answers.detail: Quick feet and used to competing, but you've never run far without a ball.
Explosive and physical, but not used to running far.
Endless sprints and changes of direction, not much running form.
Short dashes between bases, sharp reactions, little endurance.
Springy legs and good coordination, but a heavy stride.
A big engine from long winters on skis, but not much pop in your legs.
Years of running through forests: a strong engine, but no sprint.
A strong engine, but running muscles and bones aren't used to the pounding.
Strong, mobile and body-aware, but never ran far.
Light on your feet, great posture and rhythm, not much strength or engine.
Tough, disciplined and hard to break, but stiff when you run.

answers.text: Athletics school since I was little
answers.detail: You know the basics, but years of the same drills have dulled the hunger, and your body has seen it all before.
Just played outside a lot. A blank slate.
Games, books, the sofa. You start from scratch, but your body has never been trained, so it will respond fast.
You won the school cross-country run without really trying.
You came along because they did, and stayed for the fun.
It wasn't your idea at first, but the routine stuck years ago.

answers.text: A coach from your old sport
answers.detail: They said your legs were wasted in that sport.
The Olympics and World Championships lit a fire in you.
A packed stadium and blue-and-white flags. You were hooked.

answers.text: Nobody, it was your own idea
answers.detail: You turned up at the track one day and asked to join.

questions.question: What is your family's sporting background?

answers.detail: You grew up at the track, and everyone expects a lot of you.

answers.text: A parent was a top athlete in another sport
answers.detail: Good genes and high standards at home.
You've chased them around the track for years, and you hate losing.
Weekends were always active.
You found the sport on your own.

answers.text: They think sport is a waste of time
answers.detail: You'll have to prove them wrong.

answers.text: A big club with an indoor hall
answers.detail: Track sessions all year round, even in January.
Training is built into your school week (urheiluluokka), and so is the tiredness.
Snow covers the track half the year, so winters mean roads and ski trails.
Soft ground, hills and long easy runs.

answers.text: On my own around the neighbourhood
answers.detail: Nobody to correct your form, but nobody has to push you either.
You're about to start regular training for the first time.

questions.question: Compared to your classmates, you are…

answers.detail: An early developer: strong now, others will catch up.
Developing at a normal pace.
Mid growth spurt: all arms and legs, a bit clumsy for now.
Not much muscle, but you float along.
A late developer: tough now, big growth still to come.

questions.question: Before an important race, you usually…

answers.detail: Big moments bring out your best, small ones bore you.
You want to beat everyone, sometimes too badly.
Steady and reliable.
Nerves can get to you, but you prepare carefully.

answers.text: Don't really care how it goes
answers.detail: Relaxed, maybe a bit too relaxed.
Everything about competing is new to you.

questions.question: How do you do at school?

answers.detail: Good grades come easily, but school takes time.
You put the hours in, in class and out of it.
Average grades, no stress.
Sport matters more to you than school right now.
Often late, homework rarely done.
